subject: Procurement channel decision check-in — Healthlytics marketplace vs PO/card
messages:
From: Meera Shah <meera@healthlytics.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-07T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up on procurement path after demo

Thanks Laura & Ben — great demo this morning, appreciate the time. A couple items came up on our side that I wanted to flag now so procurement can start thinking about options: 

- We have a standard procurement playbook: for proofs-of-concept (small spend) we usually use corporate card; for production we prefer PO via our finance system.
- Security/compliance will want the vendor form filled (I attached the procurement checklist I usually pass along).
- We have an existing AWS footprint and marketplace preference is common, but some teams still prefer to go direct to vendors for billing flexibility.

Can you confirm: do you support starting on card and switching to AWS Marketplace later? Do you have a vendor form/packet we can share with our procurement team? Also copying our procurement alias (procure@healthlytics.com) so they can chime in.

Thanks — Meera
Meera Shah
Head of Data Platform, Healthlytics
[Attachment: procurement_req.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Meera Shah <meera@healthlytics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-07T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on procurement path after demo

Thanks Meera — quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Recap:
- Redwood supports both card-based payment (good for PoC) and invoiced PO for production/committed capacity.
- We can enable AWS Marketplace listing for the account; migration from direct billing to marketplace is supported but there are timing and entitlements to coordinate (see notes below).

Action items we can do this week:
1) Share our standard vendor packet + Redwood MSA (attached).
2) Ben will follow up with pricing scenarios: a PoC/card estimate and a PO/committed capacity SKU.
3) Confirm whether Healthlytics prefers AWS Marketplace (self-bill) or direct invoicing long-term.

Ben — can you send the pricing and vendor_form PDF to procure@healthlytics.com? Meera — once procurement shares the completed vendor form we’ll triage EULA/PO specifics.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: procure@healthlytics.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-08T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood procurement info + next steps (Healthlytics / DL-4482)

Hi Procurement team — Ben from Redwood here, looping in Laura. Per Meera’s note, attaching the vendor form and a short pricing snapshot for two paths: PoC (card) and committed capacity (PO). High level:

PoC (Card):
- Quick start, card accepted online, no PO needed; recommended for 30–90 day trials.
- We can set spending cap and tags so you can control usage.

Production (PO):
- Standard invoiced model for reserved/dedicated capacity; requires PO and signed MSA.
- We offer monthly invoicing or annual prepay for committed discounts.

Marketplace option: we support AWS Marketplace private offers and listed offers. If you purchase through Marketplace, procurement cadence is governed by AWS terms and invoicing flows through AWS. Some customers do PoC direct (card) and then convert to Marketplace private offer for production.

Attachments included: Redwood_vendor_form.pdf (filled sample), pricing_onepager.pdf (summary).

Next steps:
- If you prefer Marketplace, confirm Marketplace account ID and whether you need a private offer (we’ll coordinate with our Marketplace ops).
- If you prefer PO, send the procurement contact and the expected billing cadence (Net30/Net45).

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call with procurement to run through the vendor form.

Best —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: Redwood_vendor_form.pdf (pdf)]

From: procure@healthlytics.com
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-08T14:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood procurement info + next steps (Healthlytics / DL-4482)

Ben / Laura — thanks for the clear options. A few notes from procurement: 

- We completed the vendor form (attached).
- For initial deployment we prefer to start the PoC on corporate card, but our Finance team will require production to be on AWS Marketplace or via PO. Primary preference is AWS Marketplace (for centralized billing) but we need to understand whether we can get a private offer with the MSR/commit terms.
- Regarding EULA/terms: we will likely request a narrow redline around data retention and audit rights. Please indicate who on your legal team we should send redline suggestions to.

Attaching: procurement_packet.docx (completed).

Thanks —
Healthlytics Procurement
procure@healthlytics.com

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Meera Shah <meera@healthlytics.com>, procure@healthlytics.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-09T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood procurement info + next steps (Healthlytics / DL-4482)

Great — thanks for the packet. Quick plan to keep momentum: 

1) Start PoC on corporate card (fastest), launch next week after Meera confirms billing card.
2) Simultaneously, Finance can start Marketplace setup: if Healthlytics wants a private offer, we’ll engage Marketplace ops and our partnerships lead (Rishi is looped) to draft the private offer. Typical timeline for private offers is 2–4 weeks depending on contract review.
3) Legal redlines: please send proposed redlines to legal@redwood.com — I’ve alerted our legal ops to expect an incoming EULA redline and we’ll triage quickly.

I’ve attached a short SOW draft to outline PoC success criteria and a DocuSign link for the MSA if you want to start with a signed base agreement before production: https://www.docusign.com/agree/abc123-redwood-msa

Can procurement confirm: (a) preferred long-term billing path (Marketplace vs Invoice PO) and (b) finance contact and Marketplace account ID if you want the private offer route.

Thanks — we’ll hold on executing card transaction until Meera confirms.

Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
